claims.text: Circular OC 115F serves as an addendum to circular NPCI/UPI/OC-115E/2024-25 regarding the resolution of Numeric UPI IDs.
Banks, PSPs, and UPI Applications must utilize the Mobile Number Revocation List (MNRL) on the Digital Intelligence platform to update their databases regularly.
The liability for any omission, delay, or dispute arising from failure to update the Numeric UPI ID Mapper rests with the PSP and the UPI Application.

Payer PSPs and UPI Applications must route mobile number-based transactions through the Numeric UPI ID Mapper, except when response time exceeds one second, in which case local resolution is permitted but liability remains with the respective PSP and UPI Application.

In the interim before a separate Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is issued for user complaints regarding non-updation of UPI ID Mapper Number transactions, Remitter Banks must investigate complaints after verifying specific conditions.

The verification conditions for Remitter Banks include confirming the transaction used the Numeric UPI ID Mapper, checking if the beneficiary mobile number was present in MNRL records prior to the transaction, and determining if the Beneficiary Bank represented or rejected the chargeback request.

It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem. With this objective, NPCI will be retiring the support for CL prior to Version 1.8 after 30% September 2024. To ensure compliance PSP Banks shall certify and enable CL 1.8 or above and their respective UPI Apps shall integrate the latest version of CL within their application, on or before 30% September 2024. Bharat QR was launched on 20th February, 2017. Further, under the guidance of Indian Bank Association (IBA), NPCI had facilitated to integrate UPI credentials (Virtual Payment Address (VPA), Account + IFSC & Aadhaar number) as a part of Bharat QR standards. In this regard, NPCI had released technical specifications (Merchant QR Code Specification V 4.0) to integrate UPI credentials in Bharat QR to all RuPay acquiring member banks on 18th May, 2017. It may be noted that RuPay acquiring member banks have already started the development to integrate UPI credentials with Bharat QR and various banks are under certification with NPCI. claims.text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) explicitly exempts auto-replenishment of NETC FASTag and RuPay NCMC from the requirement to send a Pre-Debit Notification (PDN) at least 24 hours prior to debit.

quotes.quote: ## 6. Pre-transaction Notification (a) An issuer shall send a pre-transaction notification to the customer, at least 24 hours prior to the actual charge / debit.
